regions_game_px.name: far openings of the podlubie (bay 1 and, through the fence, bays 2-3)

instruction:
The picture shows the yard side of a Slovak housing-estate school on a sunny late-October afternoon in 2020 (the building renovated in light grey with white windows, simple painted motifs on the ground floor, autumn leaves). Image 2 is the SAME view with the same camera, painted for June 1995, already showing the change wanted here. Make one small local change in the right half of the picture and nothing else.

Right of the entrance canopy (about 58-75 % from the left, 30-37 % from the top) the ground floor of the long building is an open covered passage ("podlubie") on square pillars painted bright blue and green. At its far end it now shows a bright glimpse of pastel panel blocks of flats and autumn trees. That is wrong: the passage only leads into the school's own small, enclosed inner courtyard. Replace that glimpse in every opening of the passage exactly as in image 2, but in the 2020 autumn state of image 1: behind the passage lies a small sunlit inner courtyard of the school - a strip of lawn with a few fallen leaves and a few low shrubs turning yellow - and close behind it the plain renovated light-grey rendered wall of another wing of the same school, with a row of the same white-framed windows as the main building; this wall fills each far opening right up to the passage ceiling. No panel blocks of flats, no tall buildings, no sky and no distant trees in the openings. It must read as a closed little courtyard, not as a way through.

Keep everything else exactly as it is: the blue and green pillars, the dark passage ceiling, the passage side wall with its flower-and-sun motif, the passage floor, the entrance canopy and steps, the upper floors, and in front of the two right openings every post, rail and chain-link mesh panel of the dark-green fence. No people, no text.

Image 3 is another background from the same game: keep the same painting technique.

parent_prompt:
Image 1 is one of our finished point-and-click adventure game backgrounds (painted, style A). Make exactly the local changes described below and change nothing else: keep every other object, the camera, the composition, all positions, sizes, colours and the light exactly as in image 1. No people, no animals, no cars, no text, no letters, no logos, no frames. The picture shows the yard side of a Slovak housing-estate school on a sunny late-October afternoon in 2020: the building renovated in light grey with white windows and simple painted flower, sun and leaf motifs on the ground floor, autumn leaves, a football pitch with artificial turf behind the fence. Image 2 is the SAME view with the same camera, painted for June 1995, already showing exactly the two changes wanted here: copy the shape, position and size of both changes from image 2, but paint them in the 2020 state of image 1. Make the two local changes, both in the right half of the picture, and nothing else.

CHANGE 1 - lawn instead of the footpath. A grey paved footpath runs from the foot of the entrance steps (about 57 % from the left, 40 % from the top) diagonally down to the right along the LEFT side of the tall dark-green chain-link fence, and widens into the paved yard at the bottom. Remove this footpath completely. Its whole area, from the grass bank below the entrance down to the yard, becomes the same mown green lawn as the big lawn left of it (same grass colour, texture and autumn light, a few fallen yellow leaves, a few longer tufts along the fence foot), reaching right up to the bottom rail of the fence. Towards the yard the new lawn ends in a straight low concrete kerb that continues the existing kerb line along the front of the big lawn: the kerb runs level at about 59 % from the top all the way to the fence behind the green wheelie bin (as in image 2), so the lawn's diagonal corner disappears. In front of that kerb the worn grey yard asphalt stays exactly as it is. The red pipe, the green wheelie bin and every fence post, rail and mesh panel stay exactly as they are. The short paved landing at the foot of the entrance steps and the path leading from it to the LEFT stay.

CHANGE 2 - an open underpass right of the entrance, as in image 2. Image 3 is a photo of the real place in the 2020s: right of the glass entrance doors the ground floor of the long building is not a wall but an open covered passage straight through the building (a "podlubie") to the panel blocks of flats behind the school; the upper floors rest on a row of square pillars, the space between the pillars is open and the passage behind them is deep and dim; in the 2020s the pillars and the ground-floor walls are painted in bright colours (blue, green). In image 1, the three ground-floor bays right of the entrance canopy - the lower walls and the windows between the pillars, from the canopy's right edge (about 58 % from the left) to the third pillar to its right (about 75 % from the left), between about 29 % and 37 % from the top - become such an open passage exactly like in image 2: keep the pillars, the white band above them and all the upper floors exactly where they are; remove the walls and the windows between the pillars; show the dark shaded underside of the first floor as the passage ceiling, the passage floor level with the entrance landing, and at the far end of the passage a small bright opening with a glimpse of the sunlit far side: renovated panel blocks of flats in pale pastel colours with rows of windows, and autumn trees. Paint the pillars of the passage in plain bright blue and green as in image 3, and the passage side wall with one simple invented motif in the style of the flower and sun motifs of image 1 - no letters, no signs, no graffiti, no gates. Two of the three bays are seen through the court fence: keep every fence post, rail and mesh panel in front of them exactly as it is.

Image 4 is another background from the same game: keep the same painting technique. Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
